      AMGEN REPORTS THIRD QUARTER 2026 FINANCIAL RESULTS

      News provided by

      Amgen

      Nov 03, 2026, 16:01 ET

      Share this article

        •

      Share this article

        •

      THOUSAND OAKS, Calif., Nov. 3, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Amgen (NASDAQ: AMGN) today announced financial results for the third quarter of 2026.

      "Amgen delivered another strong quarter as our strategy for long-term growth continued to produce results across the enterprise," said Robert A. Bradway, chairman and chief executive officer. "The strength of our commercial portfolio, combined with important clinical advances and a promising late-stage pipeline, reinforces our confidence in Amgen's ability to deliver durable growth well into the next decade."

      Key results include:

      • For the third quarter, total revenues increased 8% to $10.4 billion in comparison to the third quarter of 2025.
        • Product sales grew 8%, driven by volume growth.
        • Seventeen products delivered at least double-digit sales growth in the third quarter.
        • Seventeen products are annualizing at more than $1 billion based on third quarter sales.
      • GAAP earnings per share (EPS) increased 19% from $5.93 to $7.08 for the third quarter, driven by higher revenues.
        • For the third quarter, GAAP operating income increased from $2.5 billion to $3.7 billion, and GAAP operating margin increased 9.9 percentage points to 37.5%.
      • Non-GAAP EPS increased 14% from $5.64 to $6.45 for the third quarter, primarily driven by higher revenues, partially offset by higher operating expenses.
        • For the third quarter, non-GAAP operating income increased from $4.3 billion to $4.7 billion, and non-GAAP operating margin increased 0.2 percentage points to 47.3%.
      • The Company generated $3.7 billion of free cash flow in the third quarter of 2026 versus $4.2 billion in the third quarter of 2025, driven by changes in working capital, with the third quarter of 2025 benefiting from the timing of rebates and collections, partially offset by current period business performance.

      References in this release to "non-GAAP" measures, measures presented "on a non-GAAP basis," and "free cash flow" (computed by subtracting capital expenditures from operating cash flow) refer to non-GAAP financial measures. Adjustments to the most directly comparable GAAP financial measures and other items are presented on the attached reconciliations. Refer to Non-GAAP Financial Measures below for further discussion.

      Product Sales Performance

      General Medicine

      • Repatha® (evolocumab) sales increased 37% year-over-year to $1,085 million in the third quarter, primarily driven by volume growth.
      • EVENITY® (romosozumab-aqqg) sales increased 39% year-over-year to $751 million in the third quarter, driven by volume growth.
      • Prolia® (denosumab) sales decreased 45% year-over-year to $632 million in the third quarter as multiple biosimilars have launched globally. The decrease was driven by 23% lower volume with the remainder driven equally by lower net selling price and changes to estimated sales deductions.

      Rare Disease

      • TEPEZZA® (teprotumumab-trbw) sales decreased 6% year-over-year to $526 million in the third quarter, driven by lower inventory levels.
      • KRYSTEXXA® (pegloticase) sales increased 31% year-over-year to $419 million in the third quarter, primarily driven by higher net selling price.
      • UPLIZNA® (inebilizumab-cdon) sales increased 191% year-over-year to $451 million in the third quarter, primarily driven by volume growth.
      • TAVNEOS® (avacopan) sales decreased 2% year-over-year to $105 million in the third quarter, driven by 9% lower volume, 8% unfavorable changes to estimated sales deductions and 5% lower net selling price, partially offset by higher inventory levels. We continue to engage with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and believe that TAVNEOS demonstrates clinical effectiveness and a favorable benefit-risk profile.

      Inflammation

      • TEZSPIRE® (tezepelumab-ekko) sales increased 43% year-over-year to $538 million in the third quarter, driven by volume growth.
      • Otezla® (apremilast) sales decreased 18% year-over-year to $481 million in the third quarter, driven by 13% lower volume, 9% unfavorable changes to estimated sales deductions and 4% lower net selling price, partially offset by higher inventory levels.
      • Enbrel® (etanercept) sales increased 5% year-over-year to $611 million in the third quarter, driven by 15% favorable changes to estimated sales deductions and 8% higher inventory levels, partially offset by 14% lower net selling price, reflecting the ongoing impact of U.S. Medicare Part D price setting effective in 2026 under the Inflation Reduction Act, and lower volume.
      • AMJEVITA® (adalimumab-atto)/AMGEVITA™ (adalimumab) sales increased 24% year-over-year to $191 million in the third quarter, primarily driven by 18% volume growth and higher net selling price.
      • PAVBLU® (aflibercept-ayyh) sales increased 41% year-over-year to $300 million in the third quarter, driven by 71% volume growth, partially offset by 18% lower net selling price.

      Oncology

      • BLINCYTO® (blinatumomab) sales increased 27% year-over-year to $496 million in the third quarter, primarily driven by volume growth.
      • IMDELLTRA® (tarlatamab-dlle)/IMDYLLTRA™ (tarlatamab) sales increased 128% year-over-year to $406 million in the third quarter, driven by volume growth.
      • Vectibix® (panitumumab) sales increased 18% year-over-year to $335 million in the third quarter, primarily driven by volume growth.
      • KYPROLIS® (carfilzomib) sales decreased 8% year-over-year to $330 million in the third quarter, primarily driven by lower volume.
      • LUMAKRAS®/LUMYKRAS™ (sotorasib) sales increased 6% year-over-year to $102 million in the third quarter, driven by 14% volume growth, partially offset by 5% unfavorable changes to estimated sales deductions and lower inventory levels.
      • Nplate® (romiplostim) sales increased 3% year-over-year to $472 million in the third quarter. U.S. government orders were $65 million in Q3'26 compared to $90 million in Q3'25. Excluding these U.S. government orders, Nplate sales increased 11% year-over-year, primarily driven by volume growth.
      • XGEVA® (denosumab) sales decreased 47% year-over-year to $288 million in the third quarter as multiple biosimilars have launched globally. The decrease was primarily driven by 32% lower volume and 11% lower net selling price.
      • MVASI® (bevacizumab-awwb) sales decreased 21% year-over-year to $168 million in the third quarter, primarily driven by 11% lower net selling price and lower volume.

      Established Products

      • Our established products, which consist of Aranesp® (darbepoetin alfa), Neulasta® (pegfilgrastim), and Parsabiv® (etelcalcetide), generated $606 million of sales in the third quarter. Sales increased 14% year-over-year, driven by 19% higher net selling price, partially offset by 3% lower volume.

      Operating Expense, Operating Margin and Tax Rate Analysis

      On a GAAP basis:

      • Total Operating Expenses decreased 5% year-over-year for the third quarter. Cost of Sales as a percentage of product sales decreased 5.5 percentage points, driven by lower amortization expense from acquisition-related assets and lower manufacturing costs, partially offset by higher profit share expense and changes in our sales mix. Research & Development (R&D) expenses increased 11% driven by higher spend in Research and Early Pipeline, including business development activity. Selling, General & Administrative (SG&A) expenses decreased 2% driven by lower general and administrative expenses, partially offset by higher commercial product-related expenses. Other operating expenses for the third quarter of 2026 totaled $76 million.
      • Operating Margin as a percentage of product sales increased 9.9 percentage points to 37.5%.
      • Tax Rate decreased 0.5 percentage points for the third quarter primarily driven by the change in earnings mix, including lower net unrealized gains on our equity investments, partially offset by net favorable items in the prior year as compared to the current year.

      On a non-GAAP basis:

      • Total Operating Expenses increased 8% year-over-year for the third quarter. Cost of Sales as a percentage of product sales increased 1.1 percentage points driven by higher profit share expense and changes in our sales mix, partially offset by lower manufacturing costs. R&D expenses increased 11% driven by higher spend in Research and Early Pipeline, including business development. SG&A expenses decreased 1% driven by lower general and administrative expenses, partially offset by higher commercial product-related expenses.
      • Operating Margin as a percentage of product sales increased 0.2 percentage points for the third quarter to 47.3%.
      • Tax Rate decreased 2.3 percentage points for the third quarter primarily driven by the change in earnings mix.

      • During the third quarter of 2026, there were no repurchases of shares of common stock under our stock repurchase program.
      • Cash and cash equivalents totaled $13.2 billion and debt outstanding totaled $54.0 billion as of September 30, 2026.

      2026 Guidance

      For the full year 2026, the Company expects:

      • Total revenues in the range of $38.9 billion to $39.7 billion.
      • On a GAAP basis, EPS in the range of $18.34 to $19.28, and a tax rate in the range of 14.5% to 16.0%.
      • On a non-GAAP basis, EPS in the range of $22.90 to $23.70, and a tax rate in the range of 15.0% to 16.5%.
      • Capital expenditures to be approximately $2.6 billion.
      • Share repurchases not to exceed $3.0 billion.

      Third Quarter Product and Pipeline Update

      The Company provided the following updates on selected product and pipeline programs:

      General Medicine

      MariTide™ (maridebart cafraglutide/AMG 133)

      • MariTide is a differentiated antibody-peptide conjugate that activates the glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor and antagonizes the glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide receptor (GIPR). MariTide's long-acting design supports starting with monthly dosing, and staying on MariTide with as few as four or six doses per year.
      • MARITIME-1, a Phase 3 study of MariTide for chronic weight management, is ongoing in adults living with obesity or overweight, without Type 2 diabetes (T2D).
      • MARITIME-2, a Phase 3 study of MariTide for chronic weight management, is ongoing in adults living with obesity or overweight, with T2D.
      • MARITIME-CV, a Phase 3 study of MariTide on cardiovascular (CV) outcomes, has completed enrollment of adults living with established atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease and obesity or overweight.
      • MARITIME-HF, a Phase 3 study of MariTide on reduction of heart failure (HF) events and cardiovascular risk, is enrolling adults living with heart failure with preserved or mildly reduced ejection fraction and obesity.
      • MARITIME-OSA-1, a Phase 3 study of MariTide, has completed enrollment of adults living with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) on positive airway pressure therapy and living with obesity or overweight.

      • In August, results from a new pre-specified analysis of the Phase 3 VESALIUS-CV pre-cardiovascular event trial on the protective effects of Repatha on fatal outcomes were presented at the European Society of Cardiology (ESC) Congress.
        • In this study, Repatha was associated with a nominal:
          • 20% reduction in all-cause mortality
          • 21% reduction in cardiovascular death
          • 15% reduction in non-cardiovascular death, largely explained by lower rates of non-fatal myocardial infarction, stroke, and ischemia-driven revascularization
        • Repatha also demonstrated that the reduction in mortality began around 1.5 years after treatment and continued through a median 4.6 years of follow-up.
      • In August, results from a new pre-specified analysis of the Phase 3 VESALIUS-CV trial on the protective effect of Repatha on total cardiovascular events were also presented at ESC Congress. In this study, Repatha:
        • reduced the total number of MACE (major adverse cardiac events), providing support for the role of intensive low-density lipoprotein cholesterol lowering to prevent first and subsequent MACE in patients at high cardiovascular risk and no prior MI or stroke
        • demonstrated a 27% relative reduction in the risk of a composite of coronary heart disease death, heart attack or ischemic stroke (3-P MACE)
        • demonstrated a 20% reduction in a broader composite that also included ischemia-driven revascularization (4-P MACE)

      • In October, the results from the Phase 3 CROSSING study of TEZSPIRE in eosinophilic esophagitis (EOE) were presented at the American College of Gastroenterology (ACG) and the United European Gastroenterology Week (UEGW). In this study, TEZSPIRE dosed every four weeks:
        • achieved histologic remission at Week 24 in 64.8% and 68.9% of EoE patients receiving the 210 mg and 420 mg doses, respectively, vs 3.5% for placebo
        • reduced the frequency and severity of dysphagia symptoms at Week 24 by 18.8 points and 22.0 points in EoE patients receiving 210 mg and 420 mg doses, respectively, vs 14.7 points for placebo, as measured by the Dysphagia Symptom Questionnaire (DSQ) score
        • sustained histological remission and continued symptom improvement through Week 52
        • achieved total endoscopic remission at Week 52 in 34.4% and 29.5% of EoE patients receiving the 210 mg and 420 mg doses, respectively, vs 4.1% for placebo
        • demonstrated a safety profile consistent with its approved indications
      • Two Phase 3 studies of TEZSPIRE are enrolling adults with moderate to very severe chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and a blood eosinophil count (BEC) ≥ 150 cells/µL.

        • achieved statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvements in disease activity by 10.2 points with low dose (6.0 points placebo-adjusted improvement) and 9.9 points with high dose (5.7 points placebo-adjusted improvement), as measured by the change from baseline of the Cutaneous Lupus Erythematosus Disease Area and Severity Index - Activity (CLASI-A) score at Week 24
        • showed statistically significant improvement in disease activity as early as Week 4 with the low dose and Week 8 with the high dose
        • demonstrated a ≥50% reduction in CLASI-A score (CLASI-50) at Week 24 in 61.7% of patients on low dose (38.0% placebo-adjusted improvement) and 62.1% of DLE patients on high dose (38.4% placebo-adjusted improvement)
        • achieved a clear or almost-clear skin at Week 24 in 60.3% of patients on low dose (51.5% placebo-adjusted improvement) and 51.6% of DLE patients on high dose (42.8% placebo-adjusted improvement), as measured by the proportion of patients achieving the Cutaneous Lupus Activity Investigator's Global Assessment (CLA-IGA 0/1)
        • demonstrated a favorable safety profile, with no serious adverse events or deaths reported

      IMDELLTRA/tarlatamab

      • IMDELLTRA is the first and only FDA-approved delta-like ligand 3 (DLL3) targeting BiTE molecule.
      • In September, the FDA approved an update to the IMDELLTRA Prescribing Information, reducing the recommended monitoring time for the first two doses from 22 to 24 hours to 6 to 8 hours from the start of infusion in an appropriate healthcare setting.
      • In September, at the World Conference on Lung Cancer (WCLC), two key IMDELLTRA results were presented:
        • A Phase 2 alternate dosing study, DeLLphi-309, evaluating IMDELLTRA dosed every three weeks or every four weeks, demonstrated durable objective response and maintained overall survival (OS) in both dosing frequencies compared to the established every 2 week dosing. Extended dosing regimens may offer flexibility in treatment combination for small cell lung cancer (SCLC) patients who are often taking other therapies
        • Results from the Phase 1b DeLLphi-308 subcutaneous administration study showed for the first time that subcutaneous IMDELLTRA can achieve comparable exposures to the intravenous route, to be further characterized in the Phase 3 DeLLphi-315 study
      • In October, three key IMDELLTRA results were presented at the European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) Congress:
        • The landmark Phase 3 DeLLphi-305 study showed that addition of IMDELLTRA to IMFINZI® (durvalumab) in first-line maintenance therapy significantly improved OS (58% reduction in risk of death) and progression-free survival (66% reduction in risk of disease progression or death) for patients who completed initial chemo-immunotherapy without progression. The DeLLphi-305 results were published simultaneously in the New England Journal of Medicine
        • IMDELLTRA continued to demonstrate a safety profile consistent with the established safety profile of IMDELLTRA in the approved second-line setting
        • A long-term update with a median follow-up of 30.8 months from the Phase 1b DeLLphi-303 first-line maintenance study, showed an estimated median OS of 37.9 months among patients that received IMDELLTRA plus a PD-L1 inhibitor as a first-line maintenance regimen following initial chemo-immunotherapy
        • A long-term update from the Phase 3 DeLLphi-304 study, which established IMDELLTRA as the standard of care for patients who have had progression on or after platinum-based chemotherapy, showed sustained OS benefit with twice as many patients alive at two years with IMDELLTRA (30%) compared to standard chemotherapy (15%). The DeLLphi-304 results were published simultaneously in Annals of Oncology
      • The Company is advancing a comprehensive, global clinical development program across extensive-stage (ES) and limited-stage (LS) SCLC:

        • DeLLphi-315, a Phase 3 study of subcutaneous tarlatamab, is enrolling patients with second-line ES-SCLC
